messages:
anya: Quick follow-up on billing attribution — we're still getting mismatches between early-tagged traces and the billing pipeline. Two obvious paths: (A) propagate a billing key from the edge through the envelope (end-to-end) or (B) keep envelopes minimal and let the enrichment service perform a late lookup. Thoughts on tradeoffs, ops risk, and sampling interplay?

ben: Short list of concerns: cardinality explosion if we let callers set arbitrary keys, KMS/privacy for real keys, cache pressure on enrichment DB, and difficulty debugging when late lookup fails.

claire: infra POV: early propagation simplifies aggregation and backfills — you can attribute at ingest time. Late lookup means an extra dependency (db/caching layer) on the hot path unless we make it async. Also need TTL semantics for keys and a plan for stale keys.

sam: SRE: if lookup is sync it will add p95 and more failure modes. If async, you lose attribution for immediate spikes. Also worry about amplification during incidents (lookup storms). We need circuit breakers + bulkhead for the enrichment DB.

telemetry-bot: FYI: ingestion schema v3.4 already includes an optional `billing_hint` field on the envelope. Docs: https://go.redwood/internal/telemetry/schemas/v3.4 (internal link)

anya: Proposal: hybrid approach — propagate a low-cardinality `billing_namespace` (cheap) from the edge + an optional opaque `billing_key` header when available. Enrichment does a best-effort lookup only when `billing_key` is missing AND sample==true. Fallback to a generic bucket `tenant:unknown` for full-traffic paths. Pseudocode for headers:

```
X-Billing-Namespace: corp
X-Billing-Key: <opaque-or-empty>
```

This lets us: (1) attribute most traffic cheaply, (2) avoid DB reads for full traffic, (3) still get high-fidelity attribution for sampled forensic traces.

ben: I like the hybrid. Additions: validate namespace values at the edge (deny arbitrary strings), enforce max cardinality, and surface metrics: `billing_key_lookup_rate`, `billing_key_lookup_missrate`.

claire: Implementation notes: sidecar/proxy can stamp `billing_namespace` with minimal cost. Enrichment should keep an LRU cache + per-tenant rate limiter and a circuit breaker. For async backfill cases we should write attribution to a side channel so downstream billing can consume later.

sam: Ops checklist: add CB with fail-open vs fail-closed policy defined per route, emit `lookup_latency` histogram, have an emergency kill switch for enrichment lookups, and run chaos test to validate amplification scenarios.

devex: I'll update the instrumentation guide + SDK examples to show `X-Billing-Namespace` and optional `X-Billing-Key`. Can we carve out 30m Thursday 10:00am to sync on RFC and rollout steps? @anya @claire @sam

anya: +1 for Thursday. I'll draft a short RFC with migration plan, metrics to track (miss rate, p95 lookup, unknown attribution fraction), and a benchmark that simulates a 10x spike to validate cache + circuit breaker behavior. :thumbsup:
